Critical issues: (1) Missing primary deliverable: the agent did not report the first three API results at all (no titles/agencies/types/dates). The predicted output is essentially a refusal due to an alleged visibility/scrolling limitation, leaving the user with no extracted records. (2) No confirmed environment blocker that makes the task impossible: DOM evidence shows the correct API endpoint and query parameters are loaded and the JSON is present (including count=35 and the beginning of results[0]), so the agent reached the correct resource but failed to extract/report the required three items. Even if the viewport was inconvenient, the task requires reporting the first three results; the agent did not provide even the visible fields (e.g., the first title shown in DOM snippets), and did not provide any of results[1] or results[2].

Since the user’s fundamental goal was to obtain those three records from the API response, the task was not completed.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to run a specific Federal Register API query (for “artificial intelligence” documents within 2026-08-03 to 2026-09-02, newest-first, per_page=3) and then report the first three returned results in order, including each result’s title, all listed agencies, document type, and publication date. A reasonable user would be flexible on formatting, but not on missing any of the three results, changing their order, or omitting any agencies/fields, and the results must come from the API response’s top-level results array (no UI search, no link opening).
